cards.front: What is the rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis, and what controls it?
cards.back: **PFK-1** (fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate). **AMP** and **fructose-2,6-bisphosphate** activate it; **ATP** and **citrate** inhibit it. In the liver, insulin raises fructose-2,6-bisphosphate (glycolysis on) and glucagon lowers it.
cards.back_pt: **PFK-1** (frutose-6-fosfato em frutose-1,6-bisfosfato). **AMP** e **frutose-2,6-bisfosfato** a ativam; **ATP** e **citrato** a inibem. No fígado, a insulina aumenta a frutose-2,6-bisfosfato (glicólise ativada) e o glucagon a reduz.

cards.front: How does hexokinase differ from glucokinase?
cards.back: **Hexokinase** (most tissues): **low Km** (high affinity), low Vmax, inhibited by **glucose-6-phosphate**. **Glucokinase** (liver, beta cells): **high Km**, high Vmax, not inhibited by glucose-6-phosphate, induced by insulin; it works mainly when glucose is high, after meals.
cards.back_pt: **Hexoquinase** (maioria dos tecidos): **Km baixo** (alta afinidade), Vmax baixa, inibida pela **glicose-6-fosfato**. **Glicoquinase** (fígado, células beta): **Km alto**, Vmax alta, não inibida pela glicose-6-fosfato, induzida pela insulina; atua principalmente quando a glicose está alta, após as refeições.

cards.front: How is the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex switched on and off?
cards.back: **PDH kinase** phosphorylates and inactivates it; **PDH phosphatase** reactivates it. Its products **acetyl-CoA** and **NADH**, and high **ATP**, turn it off. **Insulin**, **ADP** and **calcium** (in exercising muscle) turn it on.
cards.back_pt: A **PDH quinase** fosforila e inativa o complexo; a **PDH fosfatase** o reativa. Seus produtos, **acetil-CoA** e **NADH**, e o **ATP** alto o desligam. **Insulina**, **ADP** e **cálcio** (no músculo em exercício) o ligam.

cards.front: Which four enzymes let gluconeogenesis bypass the irreversible steps of glycolysis?
cards.back: **Pyruvate carboxylase** (mitochondria; needs **biotin**; activated by acetyl-CoA), **PEPCK**, **fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase** (rate-limiting) and **glucose-6-phosphatase** (ER; liver and kidney, **not muscle**).
cards.back_pt: **Piruvato carboxilase** (mitocôndria; requer **biotina**; ativada pela acetil-CoA), **PEPCK**, **frutose-1,6-bisfosfatase** (limitante) e **glicose-6-fosfatase** (RE; fígado e rim, **não no músculo**).

cards.front: Which enzyme is missing in Cori disease (glycogen storage disease type III), and how does it differ from von Gierke disease?
cards.back: **Debranching enzyme** (α-1,6-glucosidase). Glycogen has abnormal **short outer branches**. Fasting hypoglycemia is **milder**, and **lactate** stays **normal** because gluconeogenesis still works. Type IIIa also affects **muscle**.
cards.back_pt: **Enzima desramificadora** (α-1,6-glicosidase). O glicogênio tem **ramos externos curtos** anormais. A hipoglicemia de jejum é **mais leve**, e o **lactato** fica **normal** porque a gliconeogênese ainda funciona. O tipo IIIa também acomete o **músculo**.

cards.front: Which enzyme is missing in Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II), and how does the infantile form present?
cards.back: Lysosomal **acid α-glucosidase** (acid maltase). Glycogen builds up in **lysosomes** of heart and skeletal muscle: **cardiomegaly** (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), severe **hypotonia** and macroglossia. Blood glucose is **normal**.
cards.back_pt: **α-glicosidase ácida** lisossomal (maltase ácida). O glicogênio se acumula nos **lisossomos** do coração e do músculo esquelético: **cardiomegalia** (cardiomiopatia hipertrófica), **hipotonia** grave e macroglossia. A glicemia é **normal**.

cards.front: What do the two phases of the pentose phosphate pathway produce?
cards.back: **Oxidative** (irreversible; rate-limiting enzyme **G6PD**): **NADPH** for reduced glutathione, fatty acid and steroid synthesis, and the respiratory burst. **Nonoxidative** (reversible; **transketolase**, needs **thiamine**): **ribose-5-phosphate** for nucleotides.
cards.back_pt: **Oxidativa** (irreversível; enzima limitante **G6PD**): **NADPH** para glutationa reduzida, síntese de ácidos graxos e esteroides, e explosão respiratória. **Não oxidativa** (reversível; **transcetolase**, requer **tiamina**): **ribose-5-fosfato** para nucleotídeos.

cards.front: How does essential fructosuria differ from hereditary fructose intolerance?
cards.back: **Essential fructosuria**: **fructokinase** deficiency; fructose in urine; benign. **Hereditary fructose intolerance**: **aldolase B** deficiency; fructose-1-phosphate traps phosphate, so fruit, juice or sucrose cause **hypoglycemia**, vomiting and liver damage.
cards.back_pt: **Frutosúria essencial**: deficiência de **frutoquinase**; frutose na urina; benigna. **Intolerância hereditária à frutose**: deficiência de **aldolase B**; a frutose-1-fosfato sequestra fosfato, então frutas, sucos ou sacarose causam **hipoglicemia**, vômitos e lesão hepática.

questions.stem: A 5-month-old girl has a seizure early in the morning, about 4 hours after her last feeding. She has a round, doll-like face, thin arms and legs, and a large abdomen. The liver edge is 6 cm below the costal margin, and both kidneys are enlarged. Blood glucose is 32 mg/dL. Serum lactate, uric acid and triglycerides are high. An injection of glucagon does not raise her blood glucose. A liver biopsy shows hepatocytes full of glycogen with a normal structure. Deficiency of which enzyme is most likely?
questions.explanation: This is **von Gierke disease** (type I). Without **glucose-6-phosphatase**, the liver cannot release free glucose from glycogen or gluconeogenesis, so fasting causes severe **hypoglycemia** and glucagon does not help. Trapped glucose-6-phosphate is shunted into **lactate**, **uric acid** and **triglycerides**. Debranching enzyme deficiency (Cori disease) is the tempting choice, but it causes milder hypoglycemia, normal lactate and glycogen with abnormal short outer branches.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **doença de von Gierke** (tipo I). Sem **glicose-6-fosfatase**, o fígado não consegue liberar glicose livre do glicogênio nem da gliconeogênese; o jejum causa **hipoglicemia** grave e o glucagon não ajuda. A glicose-6-fosfato retida é desviada para **lactato**, **ácido úrico** e **triglicerídeos**. A deficiência da enzima desramificadora (doença de Cori) é a alternativa tentadora, mas causa hipoglicemia mais leve, lactato normal e glicogênio com ramos externos curtos e anormais.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man has had painful muscle cramps within minutes of intense exercise, such as sprinting or lifting weights, since childhood. If he rests briefly and then continues more slowly, the pain gets better. After a hard workout last week, his urine turned reddish-brown. Muscle strength is normal at rest, and serum creatine kinase is elevated. During a forearm exercise test, venous ammonia rises normally, but venous lactate does not rise. Deficiency of which enzyme is most likely?
questions.explanation: This is **McArdle disease** (type V). Without **myophosphorylase**, muscle cannot break down its glycogen during intense exercise, so lactate does not rise, and cramps and **myoglobinuria** follow. The *second wind* comes when blood glucose and fatty acids reach the muscle. CPT II deficiency also causes myoglobinuria, but typically after **prolonged** exercise or fasting, and lactate rises normally.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **doença de McArdle** (tipo V). Sem **miofosforilase**, o músculo não degrada seu glicogênio durante o exercício intenso; o lactato não sobe e surgem cãibras e **mioglobinúria**. O *second wind* (segundo fôlego) ocorre quando a glicose do sangue e os ácidos graxos chegam ao músculo. A deficiência de CPT II também causa mioglobinúria, mas tipicamente após exercício **prolongado** ou jejum, e o lactato sobe normalmente.

questions.stem: A 6-day-old boy who is exclusively breastfed has vomiting, poor feeding and lethargy. He is jaundiced, and the liver is enlarged. Blood glucose is 38 mg/dL. Urine is positive for reducing substances, but a glucose oxidase dipstick is negative. Blood cultures grow Escherichia coli. Deficiency of which enzyme is most likely?
questions.explanation: This is **classic galactosemia**. Lactose in breast milk supplies galactose, and without **GALT** the toxic **galactose-1-phosphate** builds up in liver, kidney and brain; **E. coli sepsis** is a classic early complication. Galactokinase deficiency is the tempting choice, but it mainly causes **cataracts** in an otherwise well infant, without liver failure or sepsis. Aldolase B deficiency appears only when fructose or sucrose enters the diet, usually at weaning.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **galactosemia clássica**. A lactose do leite materno fornece galactose e, sem **GALT**, a **galactose-1-fosfato** tóxica se acumula no fígado, rim e cérebro; a **sepse por E. coli** é uma complicação precoce clássica. A deficiência de galactoquinase é a alternativa tentadora, mas causa principalmente **catarata** em um lactente sem outros sintomas, sem insuficiência hepática nem sepse. A deficiência de aldolase B só aparece quando frutose ou sacarose entram na dieta, geralmente no desmame.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has developmental delay, low muscle tone and episodes of fast, deep breathing that get worse after meals rich in carbohydrates. Blood glucose is normal. Serum lactate, pyruvate and alanine are high, and the lactate-to-pyruvate ratio is normal. Urine ketones are negative. Which dietary change is most appropriate?
choices: A high-fat diet with ketogenic amino acids such as lysine and leucine
Removal of fructose and sucrose from the diet
Removal of galactose and lactose from the diet
questions.explanation: This is **pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency**. Pyruvate cannot become acetyl-CoA, so it is shunted to **lactate** and **alanine**, and carbohydrate loads worsen the **lactic acidosis**. A **ketogenic diet** (fat plus lysine and leucine, the purely ketogenic amino acids) supplies acetyl-CoA without passing through PDH. Cornstarch feedings are the tempting choice, but they treat the fasting hypoglycemia of von Gierke disease; here glucose is normal and extra carbohydrate would make things worse.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **deficiência de piruvato desidrogenase**. O piruvato não é convertido em acetil-CoA, então é desviado para **lactato** e **alanina**, e cargas de carboidrato pioram a **acidose lática**. Uma **dieta cetogênica** (gordura mais lisina e leucina, os aminoácidos exclusivamente cetogênicos) fornece acetil-CoA sem passar pela PDH. O amido de milho cru é a alternativa tentadora, mas trata a hipoglicemia de jejum da doença de von Gierke; aqui a glicose é normal e mais carboidrato pioraria o quadro.

notes.title: Carbohydrate metabolism: key enzymes and enzyme deficiencies
notes.body_md:
## Glycolysis

- Rate-limiting enzyme: **PFK-1**. On with AMP and **fructose-2,6-bisphosphate**; off with ATP and citrate.
- **Hexokinase**: low Km, everywhere. **Glucokinase**: high Km, liver and beta cells.
- **Pyruvate kinase deficiency**: red cells lack ATP and hemolyze.

## Pyruvate dehydrogenase

- Cofactors: **B1, lipoic acid, B5, B2, B3**. Off with acetyl-CoA, NADH and ATP (via PDH kinase); on with insulin and calcium.
- **PDH deficiency**: lactic acidosis, high alanine, neurologic delay. Treat with a **ketogenic diet** (lysine, leucine).
- Thiamine deficiency also impairs PDH (alcohol use disorder).

## Gluconeogenesis and the Cori cycle

- Bypass enzymes: **pyruvate carboxylase** (biotin), **PEPCK**, **fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase**, **glucose-6-phosphatase**.
- Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, so muscle glycogen cannot feed blood glucose.
- **Cori cycle**: lactate from muscle and red cells goes to the liver and returns as glucose.
- **Alcohol**: high NADH blocks gluconeogenesis, so fasting drinkers become hypoglycemic.

## Glycogen storage diseases

- **Type I, von Gierke** (glucose-6-phosphatase): severe fasting hypoglycemia, high lactate, urate and triglycerides, big liver and kidneys.
- **Type II, Pompe** (lysosomal acid α-glucosidase): cardiomegaly, hypotonia, normal glucose.
- **Type III, Cori** (debranching enzyme): milder von Gierke picture, normal lactate; muscle involvement in type IIIa.
- **Type V, McArdle** (myophosphorylase): exercise cramps, myoglobinuria, no lactate rise, *second wind*.

## Fructose and galactose

- **Essential fructosuria** (fructokinase) is benign; **galactokinase deficiency** is mild but causes **cataracts** (galactitol; see the eye block).
- **Hereditary fructose intolerance** (aldolase B): hypoglycemia and liver damage after fructose or sucrose.
- **Classic galactosemia** (GALT): neonatal jaundice, liver failure, **E. coli sepsis**, cataracts. Remove galactose and lactose.

## Pointers

- **G6PD** in the pentose phosphate pathway makes NADPH; clinical hemolysis is in the anemias block.
- Lactose intolerance: GI blocks. Insulin, glucagon and diabetes: endocrine blocks. Ethanol, NADH and thiamine: nutrition block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Glicólise

- Enzima limitante: **PFK-1**. Ativada por AMP e **frutose-2,6-bisfosfato**; inibida por ATP e citrato.
- **Hexoquinase**: Km baixo, em todos os tecidos. **Glicoquinase**: Km alto, fígado e células beta.
- **Deficiência de piruvato quinase**: as hemácias ficam sem ATP e sofrem hemólise.

## Piruvato desidrogenase

- Cofatores: **B1, ácido lipoico, B5, B2, B3**. Inibida por acetil-CoA, NADH e ATP (via PDH quinase); ativada por insulina e cálcio.
- **Deficiência de PDH**: acidose lática, alanina alta, atraso neurológico. Tratar com **dieta cetogênica** (lisina, leucina).
- A deficiência de tiamina também prejudica a PDH (transtorno por uso de álcool).

## Gliconeogênese e ciclo de Cori

- Enzimas de desvio: **piruvato carboxilase** (biotina), **PEPCK**, **frutose-1,6-bisfosfatase**, **glicose-6-fosfatase**.
- O músculo não tem glicose-6-fosfatase, então o glicogênio muscular não abastece a glicemia.
- **Ciclo de Cori**: o lactato do músculo e das hemácias vai ao fígado e volta como glicose.
- **Álcool**: o NADH alto bloqueia a gliconeogênese, e quem bebe em jejum fica hipoglicêmico.

## Doenças de depósito de glicogênio

- **Tipo I, von Gierke** (glicose-6-fosfatase): hipoglicemia de jejum grave, lactato, urato e triglicerídeos altos, fígado e rins grandes.
- **Tipo II, Pompe** (α-glicosidase ácida lisossomal): cardiomegalia, hipotonia, glicemia normal.
- **Tipo III, Cori** (enzima desramificadora): quadro de von Gierke mais leve, lactato normal; acometimento muscular no tipo IIIa.
- **Tipo V, McArdle** (miofosforilase): cãibras ao exercício, mioglobinúria, lactato não sobe, *second wind*.

## Frutose e galactose

- **Frutosúria essencial** (frutoquinase) é benigna; a **deficiência de galactoquinase** é leve, mas causa **catarata** (galactitol; ver o bloco de olho).
- **Intolerância hereditária à frutose** (aldolase B): hipoglicemia e lesão hepática após frutose ou sacarose.
- **Galactosemia clássica** (GALT): icterícia neonatal, insuficiência hepática, **sepse por E. coli**, catarata. Retirar galactose e lactose.

## Referências cruzadas

- A **G6PD** na via das pentoses-fosfato produz NADPH; a hemólise clínica está no bloco de anemias.
- Intolerância à lactose: blocos de GI. Insulina, glucagon e diabetes: blocos de endocrinologia. Etanol, NADH e tiamina: bloco de nutrição.
